The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Illinois crypto tax is impossible to enforce as written, crypto industry tells court. The legal battle to head off the crypto transaction tax in Illinois has drawn up a hefty roster of industry opposition, and they're saying the tax won't work. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

DTCC adds Solana to Wall Street tokenization plans, targeting 2027 rollout. The securities infrastructure giant plans to bring tokenized stocks, ETFs and U.S. Treasuries to Solana as it expands next year's roadmap beyond Stellar and Arc. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto for Advisors: The blockchain built to run financial markets. The report adds another detail to the day's market picture. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Jupiter adds Anchorage-backed USDGO to its $1 billion Solana lending platform. OSL offers a yield on USDGO only to professional investors, but Jupiter said its market lets other holders earn onchain at rates set by borrower demand. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The next Congress will write rules for AI and emerging tech. They should use the stuff first.. The best thing industry leaders can do is to invest the time to ensure this country’s policymakers can experience the technology they’re regulating up close, writes Allie Page, executive director of American Innovation Project. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Nvidia CEO Huang quits company he co-founded, led for 3 decades. Shares slump. CFO Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO after Huang steps down immediately as president, chief executive and board member, as shares tumble. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $71,417 with a -4.28% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,013.78 with a -3.20% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Stablecoins just got the regulatory clarity industry wanted
items.description:
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) finalized rules for implementing the landmark stablecoin legislation President Trump signed into law last year, known as the GENIUS Act. Those rules ease several proposed restrictions on how stablecoin issuers must manage their reserves, including a previous maturity limit that would have prevented issuers from holding longer-term Treasurys.

The OCC, meanwhile, left one of the biggest industry disputes over stablecoins unanswered. [...] While the GENIUS Act prevents stablecoin issuers from paying interest directly, the OCC eliminated a proposed provision that would have barred crypto exchanges and other third-party platforms from offering customers yield on their idle stablecoin balances.

Instead, the agency said it will evaluate those kinds of arrangements on an individual basis.

Read more:How to start buying crypto for $100 [...] Circle Internet Group (CRCL), the country's largest stablecoin issuer, and major crypto exchange Coinbase Global (COIN) applauded the new rules. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)

"We welcome the OCC's final rules implementing the GENIUS Act — an important milestone in translating America's leadership on stablecoin legislation into clear, durable regulatory standards," Dante Disparte, Circle's chief strategy officer and head of global policy, said in a statement.

items.title: Geopolitical risk, US–China tensions, and systemic risk in cryptocurrency markets: A regime-dependent analysis
items.description: Cryptocurrency markets have become increasingly integrated into the global financial system, yet their systemic vulnerabilities to geopolitical shocks remain poorly understood. This paper provides the first empirical analysis linking US–China tensions (UCT) to systemic risk in cryptocurrency markets. Using monthly data from August 2015 to February 2024, we measure systemic interconnectedness via a TVP-VAR Total Connectedness Index, applying linear and nonlinear ARDL frameworks to the full [...] to the full sample, as well as to bearish and bullish markets separately. The results reveal strong persistence in systemic risk. Crucially, UCT emerges as the dominant driver of contagion across all regimes, whereas general geopolitical risk (GPR) measures exhibit limited explanatory power. The nonlinear analysis uncovers symmetric long-run effects, indicating that the mere uncertainty of UCT, whether increasing or decreasing, elevates long-run systemic risk. Furthermore, lagged Bitcoin [...] lagged Bitcoin trading volume consistently exacerbates contagion across all regimes. These findings provide implications for regulators and investors, highlighting the necessity for regime-sensitive, geopolitically informed risk management strategies.

2025 was the year of dollar debasement, when fears over a captured Fed led to pressure on the dollar against the Swiss franc, while bitcoin and gold went bid. [...] Were US Treasury yields to rise sharply next year, the theme of ‘financial repression’ could re-emerge. Here the US Treasury could try to contain Treasury yields by providing regulatory incentives to banks to hold more Treasuries or put pressure on the Fed to intervene.
